faq_heading: Burnaby market stats: your questions answered

blocks.text: The boards report Burnaby in 3 parts: Burnaby East, Burnaby North and Burnaby South. In September 2026, Burnaby East had the highest all-home benchmark at $982,400 and Burnaby North the lowest at $877,100, a gap of $105,300. Over twelve months the three-part spread runs Burnaby East down 6.3%, Burnaby North down 7.4%, Burnaby South down 7.2%.
Burnaby East benchmark prices and trends, September 2026

A typical Burnaby East home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $982,400 in September 2026. That is little changed at −0.3% on the month, little changed at −1.3% over three months, down 2.7% over six months and down 6.3% over the year. Over three years it is down 14.2%, and over five years down 3.5%.
The weakest one-year move in Burnaby East was for a detached home homes at −6.7%; the strongest was a townhouse at −1.7%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,694,900) and an apartment ($708,100) is $986,800, and a townhouse ($857,900) sits $149,800 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,075,900, Burnaby East is 8.7% below. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.5% against down 6.3% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Burnaby East ranks 12 by all-home benchmark, with Port Moody above it at $1,011,500 and Burnaby South below it at $972,800.

Detached homes in Burnaby East: benchmark $1,694,900, little changed at +0.0% in a month, down 4.3% in three months, down 6.7% in six months, down 6.7% in a year, down 7.8% in three years and up 3.7% in five. That is 5.0% below the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,784,700).

Townhouse homes in Burnaby East: benchmark $857,900, little changed at +0.6% in a month, little changed at −0.7% in three months, up 1.6% in six months, down 1.7% in a year, down 5.6% in three years and up 16.2% in five. That is 15.6% below the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,016,700).

Apartment homes in Burnaby East: benchmark $708,100, little changed at +0.1% in a month, little changed at −0.2% in three months, down 2.0% in six months, down 5.5% in a year, down 11.5% in three years and little changed at −0.4% in five. That is 3.8% above the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($682,500).

blocks.text: What the Burnaby figure is
The $982,400 Burnaby East figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for September 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Burnaby?
faq.a: In September 2026, a typical Burnaby East home was $982,400, with detached at $1,694,900. In September 2026, a typical Burnaby North home was $877,100, with detached at $1,808,500. In September 2026, a typical Burnaby South home was $972,800, with detached at $1,894,600.

faq.q: Are Burnaby home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Burnaby East is down 6.3% over twelve months and little changed at −1.3% over three months. Burnaby North is down 7.4% over twelve months and down 2.5% over three months. Burnaby South is down 7.2% over twelve months and down 2.5% over three months.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out what my home is worth?
faq.a: Jared prepares a home evaluation from recent comparable sales and the condition of your home. Contact him on 604-928-1361 or through the form on this site to arrange one.
